source: User-supplied mid-conversation, attributed to th_offline_cb.py / self.all_poss_letters in github.com/chaklam-silpasuwanchai/EEG-Real-Time-Applications (Thai-P300-Speller). NOT independently fetched/verified against the actual source file in this session.
verification_todo: Confirm the 44 consonants, 15 original vowel signs, 5 tone/diacritic marks, and remaining digits 0-5 against th_offline_cb.py directly before using this for real data collection -- this project's own design doc (Sec. 0) documents a prior incident where AI-claimed 'verified' citations were fabricated. Treat this list the same way: check the source file yourself, don't trust the '_source' label alone.
deliberate_deviations_from_source: Two characters here are NOT from th_offline_cb.py and are not expected to match it: digits 6 and 7 were dropped, and ั (mai han-akat) and ็ (mai taikhu) were added in their place. This was a deliberate substitution, decided after finding both marks were missing from the reference list and are common enough in everyday Thai (วัน 'day', รัก 'love', เด็ก 'child', เย็น 'cold/evening') that their absence forced awkward, unnatural sentence choices during calibration-text design. Digits 6/7 were judged far less valuable for a communication-focused speller than these two marks. Total count is unchanged at 72 (8x9 grid), so this does not affect flash_sequence.py's checkerboard-safety math, which depends only on index parity vs. grid position, not character identity.
